description:
Archive execution refuses a repository whose citation scan universe exceeds the 512 MiB mutation capture budget, and preview over the same universe is slow and memory-hungry.

## Background

The archive planner reports a moving-path citation warning for every place a scanned file cites a relocating artifact. By default the scan roots are the development root plus the permanent paths. Execution captures every scanned file's bytes into the guarded repository image, so a development root holding gigabytes of tracked evidence fails with `captured N bytes but the maximum is 536870912` before anything is written. Preview reads the same files into memory at once, and classification re-scans every file once per moving artifact: a 3.3 GB development root needs about 6 minutes and 5.8 GB of RSS.

Citation warnings are advisory. They appear in the plan and the execution result, and no write depends on them, so they do not need to be part of the image the mutation's conflict detection covers.

## Success Criteria

- Archive execution's captured image holds only the plan's sources, destinations, markers, citing documents, and `.jit` state; citation-scan file bytes are not charged to the capture budget.
- Citation scanning holds at most one scanned file's bytes in memory at a time, in both preview and execution.
- Each scanned file is searched once for all candidate sources rather than once per moving artifact.
- Preview and execution report the same moving-path citation warnings as before for the same repository.
- The 512 MiB capture byte limit has one definition shared by every command that uses it.
- `jit archive container 6dc81018 --execute` no longer fails on the capture budget in the gf2 repository.
title: Archive execution captures the whole citation scan universe and exceeds the capture budget
